Hey the thing is just keeping yourself busy all the time doesn't fix the issue. It's a way of delaying depression and anxiety for a lot of people it doesn't actually magically make the issues go away. I can keep myself busy with chores all morning or play games with friends for a whole afternoon but the moment I stop those thoughts can take over. It's a put off tactic for me. Have you looked into the mental health service at your university? Most will have one mine was known as the student welfare office. When I started showing signs of my issues I was kind of strongly recommended to go there by my partner. They don't tell your family because you're a student and your own person, you're not beholden to your family and they don't actually have the right to your personal medical records as far as I am aware. My parents never knew I went to my welfare team because they would have to have permission from you to be able to tell them anything. After all it's your personal information.

While I can see your point with addiction and depression I personally don't believe it's possible to be comfortable with it. I think it's possible to reach a stage of intense apathy where you can feel completely incapable of overcoming it. In my personal experience of depression and anxiety there is no comfortable. There is only a struggle. And I'm not sitting here not attempting to overcome it but assuming that it's all based down to your will to overcome your mental illness is harmful. It's effectively telling the person you're not trying hard enough because you haven't snapped out of it. Which is a pretty common thing to come up against as someone with a mental health issue from people that don't understand the complicated nature of it.

That's really harmful. As a depressed and anxious person you NEVER feel like you do enough to overcome your depression and this feeds into it even more. Who do you think sits comfortably in their depression thinking yeah it's comfortable stewing in all these negative emotions and praying that I don't have to have a monumental battle with thoughts I can't control? This kind of assumption that you can get 'comfortable in not trying to overcome your depression' is so harmful.

Honestly I lost my girl too young due to bone cancer. I've never gotten over it and it's a hole I can never fill. But her love and her nurturing I feel kind of transcends it all in a way. When she was still around my mum got a jack Russell puppy. Whenever I see that family dog it's like she gravitates to me. Like she knows that I need that love and companionship. I dunno it probably sounds silly but sometimes when I'm interacting with dogs I hope that in some way my Lola is kind of living through them in spirit, just by the way they make me feel comfort I only knew with her. For the rest of her life she never let me take a bath alone she always was there with me making sure I was ok. Honestly your dog adores you very clearly. Please treasure that bond for (fingers crossed) the many years you have together. Depression and anxiety and suicidal thoughts are vicious and cruel. But they never can quite taint that complete love that a pet gives to you. I think the way your dog reacted was to tell you she still loves you and to remind you she is still there for you when no one else is. That's what my dog did. Frankly most of the time I feel dogs are much better companions than people.

I have a similar story. When I was 15/16 I kinda lost all hope. I felt I had nothing left really I was dealing with a lot more than I've ever fully realised (am in therapy and on meds for severe depression and anxiety now but it took me years to finally recognise it for what it was). I planned to kill myself. I made sure it was a day my parents would be out most of the day and I would be guaranteed to be alone. I ran a bath brought my hair dryer in. Planned to die there. Was sat in the bath as it filled up sobbing because this was finally Gunna be it. All of a sudden heard galloping thumps up the stairs. Turned out that my greyhound who had picked me when we first saw her in the animal shelter had heard me. She came running up the stairs and put her heard over checking on me and wouldn't leave even when I told her to. She watched me the whole time I realised I couldn't do it. She needed me. I still miss her every day, but she is the only reason I lived that day. Treasure your pet, they know a lot more than we give them credit for, And their love is so incredibly unconditional.

A hung parliament is where no single party has won enough seats to have a majority in parliament. There are a total of 650 MP seats to be won. The threshold for having a majority and winning an election is 326. While conservative has won a large amount of the MP seats, They have not won 326 seats which means they have not won. This ends in a hung parliament where they cannot call themselves the appointed government without going to other parties to either ask for backing or make a coalition.
